action: If you booked a national park campsite or vehicle permit through Queensland, Victoria, South Australia or ACT systems, treat unexpected emails or calls about bookings with caution, as the ACT government urges, and do not share payment details in response.
date_note: Queensland and other agencies first disclosed the Bookeasy hack on 12 November (ABC, 12 Nov); dated by the ACT government disclosure reported by ABC on 14 November.
exec: A hack at a shared booking provider exposed customer contact and booking details across several Australian government park and tourism systems.
geo_basis: agency: Queensland Department of Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation, Brisbane
plain: A company that runs booking systems for Australian national parks was hacked. Contact and booking details may have been accessed, and customers are warned to watch for scam messages.

key_findings: Queensland's environment department told the ABC that third-party provider Bookeasy had been hacked.
Bookeasy said it was continuing to investigate and had identified potential compromising of customers' personal and booking information; it had not detected any access to credit card details.
The ACT government emailed about 6,000 users warning of scam or phishing attempts and temporarily disabled the platform.

summary: Queensland's environment department told the ABC that booking provider Bookeasy had been hacked. Bookeasy said it identified potential compromising of customers' personal and booking information and had not detected access to credit card details. Parks Victoria suspended new campsite bookings, and the ACT government, which emailed about 6,000 users about scam risk, temporarily disabled its platform.
title: Bookeasy hack hits national park booking systems in Queensland, Victoria, South Australia and ACT

validation.note: Both pages read are ABC News; Bookeasy and agency statements are quoted by ABC. The Courier Mail article on permit-free access in Queensland could not be fetched and is not used.
